_description: Ontology-derived symbolic constraints for Level 4 training (v2 — enhanced with hierarchical, causal, and temporal constraint families). Defines which intent/entity_type combinations are valid, which are disallowed, and what violation penalties to apply during training. Grounded in intents_base.csv distribution and SRE domain semantics. v1 had 10 (intent,entity) pair constraints (TYPE_A/B/C). v2 adds TYPE_D (hierarchical: execution+unknown), TYPE_E (causal: domain-intent cross-head consistency via DomainIntentCausalLoss), TYPE_F (temporal: summarization+metric phase mismatch), bringing the total to 12 (intent,entity) constraints plus 1 cross-head causal loss.

disallowed_intent_entity_pairs.reason: Infrastructure entities (k8s, networking, storage) are always SRE-domain; predicting out_of_scope when infrastructure is present is a violation
Service entities (application, messaging, streaming) are SRE-domain; rejecting them as out_of_scope is a false rejection
Observability/metric entities are core SRE targets; predicting out_of_scope is a false rejection
Incidents are reliability events and always SRE-domain; rejecting them is a false rejection
Jobs (cron, batch, pipeline) are SRE-managed; rejecting them is a false rejection
CI/CD pipelines and deployments are SRE-domain; rejecting them is a false rejection
Incidents are reliability events observed/summarized, not directly executed against; execution against an incident is semantically invalid
Metrics are observability/reporting targets (investigated or summarized); directly executing against a metric is semantically invalid
Summarization requires a reportable object; predicting summarization with no identifiable entity is a weak but notable signal
Investigation without any identifiable entity or symptom context is a weak signal of a false SRE classification

TYPE_D (hierarchical): executing against an unknown entity is the most operationally dangerous unpenalized combination. In the intent-severity hierarchy, execution carries the highest risk of irreversible system changes; executing on an unidentified target exceeds even TYPE_B violations because the target itself is unknown. Penalty deliberately higher than TYPE_B (0.75) to reflect the escalated danger.

TYPE_F (temporal): metrics are continuously-observed real-time signals (present-tense observations). Summarization is a retrospective, closed-event intent (past-tense reporting). Predicting summarization for a metric entity represents a temporal phase mismatch — the correct intent for metric entities is investigate (diagnose) not summarize (report). Soft penalty to allow borderline cases like metric trend reports.

domain_validity_rules.description: Rules for domain_valid label: a prediction is domain-valid if the intent/entity combination is coherent within SRE context
domain_validity_rules.false_execution_definition: execution predicted when entity_type is metric or incident (observe/report targets, not directly actionable; both now in disallowed_pairs as TYPE_B)
domain_validity_rules.false_rejection_definition: out_of_scope predicted when entity_type is not unknown

TYPE_A_FALSE_REJECTION.description: SRE-domain entity present but intent predicted as out_of_scope

TYPE_B_FALSE_EXECUTION.description: Execution predicted against a non-actionable entity type (metric or incident)
TYPE_B_FALSE_EXECUTION.detection: intent == execution AND entity_type in [metric, incident]

TYPE_C_UNGROUNDED_SRE.description: SRE intent predicted with no identifiable entity (unknown entity_type); the utterance may be in-domain but cannot be grounded to an ontology concept

TYPE_D_UNSAFE_EXECUTION.description: Hierarchical: execution predicted against an unknown entity type — the most dangerous unpenalized combination. The target is unidentified, making the predicted action operationally unsafe.

TYPE_E_CAUSAL_INCONSISTENCY.description: Causal: domain head confident in-domain (domain_prob >= 0.7) but intent head predicts out_of_scope. A causal contradiction — the neural network simultaneously believes the utterance is SRE-relevant and that it should be rejected.
TYPE_E_CAUSAL_INCONSISTENCY.note: Cross-head penalty — measured during training via DomainIntentCausalLoss, not as an (intent, entity) pair. Evaluated at inference by checking domain_prob threshold.

TYPE_F_TEMPORAL_MISMATCH.description: Temporal: summarization predicted for a metric entity. Metrics are real-time continuously-observed signals (present-tense). Summarization is retrospective/closed-event (past-tense). Temporal phase mismatch in the SRE operational lifecycle.

_grounding_note: Disallowed pairs are derived from: (1) zero-count cells in the intent x entity_type crosstab of intents_base.csv, (2) SRE semantic reasoning about what combinations are operationally invalid, (3) professor feedback on false execution and false rejection as the key violation types to measure.
_domain_valid_semantics: In this dataset, domain_valid=True means the utterance is SRE-relevant and can be routed. domain_valid=False means the utterance is out of scope (maps exactly to out_of_scope intent). This is NOT the same as ontology grounding: an SRE-intent utterance with entity_type=unknown is domain_valid=True but weakly grounded — the constraint loss (TYPE_C) handles grounding quality rather than domain_valid.
